metaDescription: Six compact ultrasonic cleaners for jewelry, glasses and retainers compared on frequency, tank size and timers, plus which items each one can handle.
introParagraphs: An ultrasonic cleaner drives tiny bubbles across a water bath so that grime lifts out of crevices a brush cannot reach. Near the top of this budget you find two distinct families: jewelry and eyeglass tubs with a 600ml stainless tank, and small retainer pods with UV lights and a few hundred milliliters of water. Which family you need depends entirely on what you plan to clean.

We evaluated each unit from its published specifications and the way the maker describes it, and we did not run hands-on trials. Frequency, tank volume, timer options and weight are the specs that separate these machines, so the guide leans on those figures and flags where a listing leaves a gap.

A note on expectations. These are household tools, so they loosen oils, dust and residue but do not polish metal or remove tarnish, and the UV lights some models add are a bonus rather than a replacement for rinsing and brushing. With that in mind, here is what each pick does best.

products.name: Magnasonic 20oz Ultrasonic Cleaner with 5 Cycles
products.description:
The Magnasonic is the best all-rounder in this price band. A 600ml stainless tank is roomy enough for a pair of glasses or a handful of rings in one cycle, and five preset cycles with a digital timer take the guesswork out of how long to run each load. The 42,000 Hz output is moderate, which suits everyday jewelry.

A basket is included, so items sit off the tank floor and lift out easily without fishing in the bath. That small accessory matters more than it sounds, because it keeps fine pieces from rubbing the metal and makes draining simple. The weak spots are honest ones: there is no heater, so greasy items rely on time and a drop of mild detergent, and the listing says it will not remove tarnish.

In practice it is a set-and-forget machine for weekly jewelry and glasses. Compared with the OSLTWI at 48 kHz, it offers a larger tank and more cycles, while the OSLTWI is gentler and lighter. Compared with the Ukoke, it adds a basket and cycle presets but matches the tank size.
products.bestFor: Households that want a roomy tank, simple timer presets and a basket.

600ml tank fits glasses or several rings
Included basket lifts items out cleanly
42,000 Hz suits everyday jewelry
cons: No heater for greasy or oily items

products.name: OSLTWI 48kHz Ultrasonic Jewelry Cleaner
products.description:
OSLTWI is the compact choice, weighing only 0.57 kg and carrying a 350ml 304 stainless tank. Its 48 kHz frequency is higher than the 42,000 Hz of the Magnasonic and Ukoke, which tends to be gentler on fine pieces like earrings and watch bands. A single selector switches between two cleaning modes.

The lightness is the practical appeal. It tucks into a drawer between weekly uses and moves easily to the sink for filling and draining. The limit is volume, since 350ml will not take dentures, tools or larger glasses frames, and with only two modes you get less control than a five-cycle machine. The listing does not detail a timer or heater.

The maker also claims water-only cleaning, so you can start without buying solution, though a drop of mild detergent still helps with oils. Compared with the Magnasonic, it is smaller and simpler. Compared with the COBEEK at 50 kHz, it gives up the UV light and extra timer steps but weighs less and stays cleaner to store.
products.bestFor: Light-use owners cleaning earrings, watch bands and small pieces.

products.name: COBEEK 50kHz Ultrasonic Cleaner with UV Light
products.description:
COBEEK pairs a 50 kHz ultrasonic output with a UV light and a 24oz stainless tank. Two simple buttons select among five timed cycles of 90, 180, 280, 380 and 480 seconds, which gives it the widest spread of run times in the group. Four non-slip rubber feet keep the unit steady while it hums.

The 50 kHz frequency is the highest here, so cleaning is fine-grained and gentle on delicate settings, while the 24oz tank handles glasses and several rings together. The UV light is an extra layer, but it does not replace rinsing or brushing, and it will not change how well the ultrasonic part dislodges grime. The listing positions it for jewelry, glasses and dentures alike.

Use is straightforward: add water, set a cycle and press start. Compared with the Magnasonic, it adds UV and a wider timer range but no included basket is listed. Compared with the Ukoke, it offers a higher frequency and extra timer steps in a similar size.
products.bestFor: Owners who want fine timer control and a UV light on top.

products.name: Ukoke UUC06S 42kHz Ultrasonic Cleaner
products.description:
The Ukoke UUC06S offers the same 42 kHz output and 600ml stainless tank as the Magnasonic and is positioned for jewelry, eyeglasses, rings and watches. The maker also says it can serve as a denture and retainer cleaner, which broadens its use to the whole household. It is described as portable and sized for a countertop.

A 600ml tank is the sweet spot for this budget, large enough for glasses and small enough to fill from the tap in seconds. The listing text we reviewed gives less information about timers, cycle presets and accessories than the Magnasonic, so check the full page before buying if those matter. The 360 degree cleaning claim describes the way waves reach all sides of an item.

It is a straightforward choice when you want a mid-size tank and one machine for several kinds of item. Compared with the Magnasonic, it states fewer controls. Compared with the Eonini, it suits larger items like eyeglasses that a 180ml pod cannot hold.
products.bestFor: General household use across glasses, rings, watches and dental items.

products.name: UMPOPO 48kHz UV-C Retainer Cleaner
products.description:
UMPOPO is built for oral appliances and rates itself under 38 dB, which makes it the quietest unit in this guide. It combines 48 kHz ultrasonic cleaning with a UV-C lamp, and one deep cycle runs 10 minutes of ultrasonic cleaning followed by 10 minutes of UV-C. A pulse-flow mode alternates working and resting phases during a cycle.

The 48 kHz output is gentle enough for aligners, braces and dental trays, and the low noise suits a bathroom shared with sleeping family members. The caveats are in the listing: it gives no tank volume, so judging fit is guesswork, and its mode count is stated inconsistently, so verify what you get. There is also no warranty detail, unlike some rivals.

It works best as a nightly retainer or aligner companion rather than a jewelry cleaner. Compared with the Eonini, it states a noise figure and a pulse-flow cycle where the Eonini provides a removable water tank. Compared with the Magnasonic, it is for a different job entirely.
products.bestFor: Aligner and retainer owners who want quiet operation.

10 minute clean plus 10 minute UV-C cycle
Pulse-flow mode alternates work and rest
48 kHz is gentle on aligners and braces
cons: Listing gives no tank volume for fit checks
No accessory or warranty term is listed

products.name: Eonini 45kHz Retainer Cleaner with Removable Tank
products.description:
Eonini stands out for its removable inner water tank, which makes filling and emptying simple and keeps water from leaking into the base. It runs at 45 kHz with four UV lights, and a bottom-mounted fan helps the unit shed heat during repeated cycles. It is listed for aligners and mouth guards.

The removable tank is the real convenience feature. You can carry it to the sink, rinse it thoroughly and return it, which helps with hygiene and avoids splashes on the counter. At 180ml, it holds one appliance at a time, so it is not meant for bulky items. The listing text gives no wattage, timer detail or warranty term.

It makes sense for someone who cleans a single retainer daily and wants fuss-free water changes. Compared with the UMPOPO, it adds a removable tank but states no noise figure. Compared with the Ukoke, it is much smaller and aimed at dental items instead of eyeglasses.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Frequency affects how aggressively the bubbles clean. The OSLTWI runs at 48 kHz, the COBEEK at 50 kHz, the Magnasonic and Ukoke at 42 kHz and the Eonini at 45 kHz. Higher frequencies are generally gentler on fine settings, while lower ones are a bit more forceful. For earrings and watch bands, lean toward 48 kHz or higher.

The tank decides which items can go in. The Magnasonic and Ukoke have 600ml, the COBEEK has 24oz, the OSLTWI has 350ml and the Eonini has 180ml. Eyeglasses need at least 600ml, while a retainer fits in 180ml. Measure the largest item you plan to clean before buying.

Presets prevent over- or under-running a load. The Magnasonic offers five cycles with a digital timer, and the COBEEK offers five times from 90 to 480 seconds. The OSLTWI has only two modes. If you clean varied items, favor a model with several steps.

buyingCriteria.criterion: UV light and what it adds
buyingCriteria.explanation: UV lights are a secondary feature, not a cleaning method on their own. The COBEEK, UMPOPO and Eonini include UV, while the Magnasonic, OSLTWI and Ukoke do not. UV should not replace rinsing or brushing. Treat it as a bonus for dental items rather than a reason to buy.

These machines hum, and some are louder than others. The UMPOPO lists under 38 dB, which is the only figure stated in this guide. The other listings do not give a number. If the unit will run in a bedroom or shared bathroom, quiet matters.

A cleaner you can store easily gets used more. The OSLTWI weighs 0.57 kg, which fits in a drawer, while the 600ml models are bulkier. Think about where you will keep it and where you will fill it. If you clean weekly, a drawer-friendly size wins.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared tank volume and what each unit can hold. The Magnasonic and Ukoke lead at 600ml, followed by the COBEEK at 24oz. The Eonini scored lowest for capacity because its 180ml tank holds one item.

howWeEvaluated.title: Control and presets
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at timers and modes. The Magnasonic and COBEEK lead with five steps each, while the OSLTWI offers two. Listings that mention no timer detail lost points.

howWeEvaluated.title: Gentleness
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered frequency as a proxy for suitability on delicate items. The COBEEK at 50 kHz and OSLTWI at 48 kHz lead. The 42 kHz units scored slightly lower for fine settings.

howWeEvaluated.title: Extras and convenience
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted baskets, UV lights, removable tanks and fans. The Magnasonic earned credit for its basket, the Eonini for its removable tank and the UMPOPO for its noise rating.

howWeEvaluated.title: Portability and storage
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed size and weight. The OSLTWI at 0.57 kg leads, and the retainer pods follow. The 600ml models are the bulkiest but the most capable.

faq.q: Can I clean everything in an ultrasonic cleaner?
faq.a: No. Soft stones, pearls and some coatings can be damaged. The Magnasonic listing also notes it will not remove tarnish from silver. When unsure, test a hidden area or check the maker's guidance.

Water works for light soil, and the OSLTWI listing promotes water-only cleaning. A drop of mild detergent helps with oils, especially on units without a heater. Avoid harsh chemicals unless the maker approves them.

faq.q: Do UV lights make dental items safe?
faq.a: UV lights are a bonus step and not a replacement for rinsing and brushing. The COBEEK, UMPOPO and Eonini include UV. Treat them as a convenience, not a guarantee.
The UMPOPO lists under 38 dB, the only noise figure in this guide. The others do not state a number. If noise matters, choose the UMPOPO.
Many people do, using a tank of at least 600ml. The Magnasonic, Ukoke and COBEEK have the capacity. Check lens coating guidance first and use the shortest cycle.

faq.q: How long should a cycle run?
faq.a: Short cycles are often enough, from 90 seconds for light dust. The COBEEK offers times up to 480 seconds and the Magnasonic offers five presets. Run longer only for stubborn residue.

faq.q: Where should I put the unit?
faq.a: Place it on a flat, stable surface near a sink. The COBEEK has four non-slip feet, which helps. Empty and dry it after each use.
